The chart app has two direct callers of `useAbortController`, and one indirect path through `useOpenmrsSWR`. The hook is defined in `openmrs-esm-core`, so I only read it from there; the chart checkout was searched locally.

**Direct callers (confirmed):**

1. **Vitals & biometrics form**: `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-vitals-app/src/vitals-biometrics-form/exported-vitals-biometrics-form.workspace.tsx`. It declares the controller at line 87, passes it to `createOrUpdateVitalsAndBiometrics` at line 231, and lists it in the submit callback's dependencies at line 267. This is the real dependent: a change in how the controller is created, reused, or aborted directly changes whether a save can be cancelled or reused across submits.
2. **Lab results form**: `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-orders-app/src/lab-results/exported-lab-results-form.workspace.tsx`. It declares the controller at line 70, but the local search found no other use of it in this file. It is affected only in the trivial sense that the hook is called; no request uses its signal.

**Indirect caller (confirmed through the core hook):**

3. **Person attributes hook**: `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-banner-app/src/hooks/usePersonAttributes.ts` line 16 calls `useOpenmrsSWR`. That hook calls `useAbortController` internally when no `abortController` or `fetchInit.signal` is supplied (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-react-utils/src/useOpenmrsSWR.ts` lines 70–87), so its fetches inherit whatever the hook does.

**Core definitions the above depend on:**

- `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-react-utils/src/useAbortController.ts` lines 25–38: the hook itself. It replaces the controller when the previous one is aborted and aborts on unmount.
- `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-react-utils/src/useOpenmrsSWR.ts` lines 70–87: the wrapper that consumes it.

**Not in the chart app, but in core:** `openmrs-esm-core/packages/apps/esm-primary-navigation-app/src/components/change-language/change-language.modal.tsx` line 33 also uses the hook. It is outside the scope of the question.

**Not checked:** the core mocks (`mock.tsx`, `mock-jest.tsx`) stub the hook for tests, so a behaviour change would not show up in chart tests that rely on those mocks. I did not check any dynamic or re-exported usages beyond the grep and symbol lookups.
